claim_text: The skill-creation skill orchestrates skill and slash-command authoring as know, then ask, then route, then build, owning everything up to the moment the artifact is written, while skill-creator owns the writing, the iteration, and whatever verification the user wants.
evidence_span: The orchestrator for authoring a skill or slash command: **know, then ask, then route, then build**. It owns everything up to the moment the artifact gets written; `skill-creator` owns the writing, the iteration, and whatever verification the user wants.

claim_text: A skill is a trigger plus a body that loads on demand: the description decides whether it ever fires and the body is what the model reads once it does, two separate problems each with its own way of being wrong.
evidence_span: A skill is a **trigger plus a body that loads on demand**. The `description` decides whether it ever fires; the body is what the model reads once it does. Two separate problems, each with its own way of being wrong.

claim_text: Authoring a skill from memory produces generic procedure such as "handle errors appropriately" instead of the specific formats, gotchas, and conventions that make a skill worth loading, which is why the reference knowledge loads before anything is asked or written.
evidence_span: Authoring a skill from memory produces generic procedure — "handle errors appropriately" — instead of the specific formats, gotchas, and conventions that make a skill worth loading; that's why the knowledge loads first.

claim_text: A skill built on a half-understood request encodes the misunderstanding permanently at every future invocation, so skill-creation invokes the grilling skill and writes nothing while any branch of the question tree is still open.
evidence_span: And a skill built on a half-understood request encodes the misunderstanding permanently, at every future invocation; that's why the grilling has to finish before anything is written.

claim_text: Before asking anything, skill-creation reads the archived Agent Skills specification, best-practices, and optimizing-descriptions docs plus the Claude Code skills doc and the prompting guide for the current model, and a missing doc is ingested with /llm-wiki:ingest rather than substituted from memory.
evidence_span: A doc is missing → `/llm-wiki:ingest <url>` before continuing; don't substitute memory for the reference.

claim_text: Skill-creation routes before building: a slash command when the user drives it by typing /name as a single prompt with no bundled files, a skill when Claude should reach for it on its own or it needs references/, scripts/, or assets/, a subagent via meta-agent for delegated context-isolating work, a path-scoped rule for a constraint tied to certain files, and a hook or permission rule for anything that must always or never happen.
evidence_span: | **Hook or permission rule** | Something that must always or never happen. An instruction is a preference; only the harness is a guarantee |

claim_text: Commands and skills are the same mechanism in current Claude Code — both produce /name and take the same frontmatter — so choosing between .claude/commands/<name>.md and .claude/skills/<name>/SKILL.md is a layout choice, and shipping both under one name is a mistake because the same-name skill silently beats the flat command.
evidence_span: Commands and skills are the same mechanism in current Claude Code — both produce `/name` and take the same frontmatter — so the first two rows are a layout choice, not a capability one. **Never ship both names**: a same-name skill silently beats the flat command.

claim_text: A skill with side effects such as /commit, /deploy, or /send-* is given disable-model-invocation: true so only the user can fire it.
conditions: the skill has side effects such as committing, deploying, or sending
evidence_span: A skill with side effects (`/commit`, `/deploy`, `/send-*`) gets `disable-model-invocation: true`, so only the user can fire it.

claim_text: House conventions for a produced skill: name is kebab-case and matches the directory exactly, the folder carries the namespace so filenames never echo it, bundled paths resolve through ${CLAUDE_SKILL_DIR}, and the body states what to do rather than why a design was chosen.
evidence_span: - `name` is kebab-case and matches the directory exactly. - The folder carries the namespace — don't echo it in filenames. - Bundled paths resolve through `${CLAUDE_SKILL_DIR}`.

claim_text: A new skill lands in project scope at .claude/skills/<name>/ unless the user's phrasing means it is personal, which puts it in ~/.claude/skills/<name>/, and it is committed on a feat/<slug> branch — a single self-contained skill needs no issue unless the user wants a PR.
evidence_span: Project scope — `.claude/skills/<name>/` — unless the user's phrasing means it's personal, which puts it in `~/.claude/skills/<name>/`. Ask when that's unclear.
